questions.stem: All of the following statements are true except?

options.label: A
options.text: Chronic infection of Fasciola hepatica can cause hepatocellular carcinoma

options.label: B
options.text: Paragonimus westermani infection causes endemic hemoptysis

options.label: C
options.text: Schistosoma is a trematode that lays nonoperculated eggs

options.label: D
options.text: Schistosoma has only one intermediate host, unlike other trematodes

questions.answerText: Chronic infection of Fasciola hepatica can cause hepatocellular carcinoma
questions.solutionHtml:
Chronic infection of Fasciola hepatica can cause hepatocellular carcinoma
  • Fasciola hepatica is a liver fluke that can cause cholecystitis and cholangitis. It is not associated with hepatocellular carcinoma.
  • Clonorchis sinensis is an inhabitant of the bile duct & is associated with Cholangiocarcinoma.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 735

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct pair regarding trematodes:I) Schistosoma-blood fluke-snail (intermediate host) II) Paragonimus westermani-intestinal fluke-snail & fish (intermediate host) III) Fasciola hepatica-liver fluke-snail & aquatic plants (intermediate host) IV) Fasciola buski-lung fluke-snail & aquatic plants (intermediate host)Select the correct option from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
Only I, III
  • Schistosoma is a blood fluke with a snail as an intermediate host.
  • Fasciola hepatica is a liver fluke with snails and aquatic plants as intermediate hosts.
  • Fasciola buski is an intestinal fluke with snails and aquatic plants as the intermediate host.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 735/734

questions.stem: A traveler presents with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. On investigations, an egg was found in his biliary tract. The likely organism is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Clonorchis sinensis
  • Clonorchis sinensis eggs.
  • Clonorchis sinensis eggs are small.
  • The eggs are oval-shaped with a convex operculum that rests on visible “shoulders” at the smaller end of the egg. At the opposite (opercular) lot, a small knob or hook-like protrusion is often visible.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 734

questions.stem: Liver is the primary target in-
questions.solutionHtml:
Clonorchis sinensis
  • Clonorchis sinensis, the Chinese liver fluke, belongs to the class Trematoda, phylum Platyhelminthes. It infects fish-eating mammals, including humans.
  • Clonorchiasis is an infectious disease caused by the Chinese liver fluke, Clonorchis sinensis, and two related species.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 734

questions.stem: Operculated eggs are seen on microscopy of a fresh stool sample. Which of the following can be ruled out?
questions.solutionHtml:
Schistosoma mansoni
  • Lays non-operculated eggs with the lateral spine.
  • Schistosoma mansoni is a water-borne parasite of humans, and belongs to the group of blood flukes.
  • The adult lives in the blood vessels near the human intestine.
  • It causes intestinal schistosomiasis. Clinical symptoms are caused by the eggs.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 735

questions.stemHtml: Stool examination shows the eggs (140 X 80 microns) shown in the Image. Diagnosis is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fascioliasis

The given image shows an operculated egg characteristic of Fasciola (trematode).



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 735
